answer: Each close, the verifier walks the attestation graph: it picks an attester at random, then takes a k-hop wander through the heads that attester signed for. At every stop the visited identity must re-sign the live epoch seed, or its bonded prism is slashed and the walk ends. Each stop is revealed only when reached, so a clone farm cannot pre-warm a subset — it must keep every head live at every depth. The sonnet is the line of fresh signatures the walk collects, one per stop; a fleet rerouting one shared head across stops fails the stop test. Liveness cost lands per identity, never pooled.
